Track record

The projects behind our figures. All were delivered by our founding team through the company they built before NextGenergy; none is presented as a NextGenergy installed base.

Nearly 1,000 MWOur founding team has delivered nearly 1,000 MW of liquid cooling.Condition: Cumulative capacity of liquid-cooling equipment (immersion and direct-to-chip systems, CDUs and heat-recovery units) delivered by the founding team through the company they built before NextGenergy, counted to the first quarter of 2026 and rated by the IT heat load it serves; equipment delivered, not capacity currently in operation, and not a NextGenergy installed base; not third-party audited.

Representative projects

Each project is described in the same six fields. Locations and clients are not named. 2024Asia, above 3,000 m altitudeNot published

Heat reuse · space heating

Project conditions
Above 3,000 m altitude, Asia, 2024. Capacity not published; location and client not named.
Scope of delivery
Heat-reuse system with a redesigned CDU, delivered by the founding team through their earlier company. Other scope: explained under a non-disclosure agreement.
System architecture
Waste heat used for space heating. When the heating side needed a higher supply temperature in cold weather, the CDU was redesigned with a tighter approach temperature, so the loop could deliver warmer water without running the chips hotter.
Key operating conditions
The approach temperature before and after the redesign, and the supply temperature reached: explained under a non-disclosure agreement.
Operating observation period
In the project year 2024; the operating record and its dates: explained under a non-disclosure agreement.
System diagrams and acceptance records
Not published; explained under a non-disclosure agreement.
